vision.instructions: A streamer is talking to their AI co-host. Decide whether the co-host needs to look at the streamer's screen to answer this message well.

criteria.look: The message is about something visible on the screen right now, such as the game, an image, a video, a menu or on-screen text.
criteria.no_look: The message can be answered well without seeing the screen.

memory.instructions: A streamer is talking to their AI co-host. Decide whether answering this message well needs the co-host to recall earlier conversations or facts about the streamer.

criteria.recall: The message refers to the past, to the streamer's life, preferences or plans, or to something the co-host may already know about them.
criteria.skip: The message can be answered well from the current conversation alone.

reply_length.instructions: A streamer is talking to their AI co-host. Decide how long the co-host's spoken reply to this message should be.

criteria.short: One short sentence is enough, such as for a greeting, a reaction or a quick acknowledgement.
criteria.medium: Two or three sentences, for a normal conversational reply.
criteria.long: A longer reply, for an explicit request to explain, list, compare or go into detail.

respond.instructions: A viewer wrote this message in a live stream chat. Decide whether the stream's AI co-host should answer it out loud.

criteria.respond: The message invites an answer, such as a question, a greeting to the co-host or a comment worth reacting to.
criteria.ignore: The message does not need an answer from the co-host.
